editorialNarrative.hook: LASK's five-goal comeback from a 3–0 first-leg deficit supplied the defining route into a seven-club qualifying class.
editorialNarrative.synopsis: Qualification filled the final seven places in the 36-team league phase, with LASK producing the stage's lasting recovery: a 5–1 extra-time return-leg win after losing 3–0 at Celtic. Sabah and Slovan Bratislava also survived extra time, and all seven winners now persist as named entrants in the next phase rather than disappearing with the completed bracket.

editorialNarrative.hook: AEK and LASK carry qualification straight into opening night, as Paris begins a rare chase for a third consecutive title.
editorialNarrative.synopsis: The league phase asks each of 36 clubs to face eight different opponents across 144 matches. AEK Athens v LASK opens a direct line from qualification, while first-time Champions League entrant LASK and first-time European participant Como enter the same table as back-to-back champion Paris Saint-Germain. The opening story is continuity, not a blank group-stage reset.

editorialNarrative.hook: Eight clubs skip February; sixteen must survive it; twelve leave Europe before the road to Madrid narrows.
editorialNarrative.synopsis: The 36-team league table determines three distinct fates and also shapes play-off seeding. The knockout path begins in February and ends at Estadio Metropolitano, while Paris's pursuit of a third consecutive title remains a live thread rather than an assumed participant outcome.
